name: Control estate
description: Six hundred applications, typed, and twelve security controls, each its own daily file covering only the applications it applies to, with statuses in four words; five of the controls run on SLAs with due dates that cluster, so a pass rate can flip for a day without anything being wrong. A synthetic feed from a fixed seed (scripts/data/estate.ts) with three layers of trouble planted in March 2024: the obvious (a file with no rows, a column missing, a pass rate that collapses, a scanner outage, rows twice), the contradictions and scope (key rotation passing where encryption at rest fails; WAF rows for applications that aren't internet-facing; TLS rows missing for one business unit) and the look-alikes (due dates that cluster, with the usual share running late) beside one SLA day that is a real problem (six in ten DR exercises late). What the flow says of each is the next ADR's question.

sources.description: The application inventory: unit, criticality, exposure, data classification, datastore, hosting and lifecycle
Transport encryption on internet-facing applications: the protocol offered and the certificate's days left. One row an application it applies to (internet-facing applications).
A web application firewall in front of internet-facing applications, in blocking mode, with a current ruleset. One row an application it applies to (internet-facing applications).

A penetration test within the year, for internet-facing applications of high or critical criticality. One row an application it applies to (internet-facing applications of high or critical criticality).
Encryption of data at rest, for applications with a datastore. One row an application it applies to (applications with a datastore).
Encryption keys rotated within the year, for regulated data at rest; it needs encryption at rest. One row an application it applies to (applications with regulated data in a datastore).
Backups taken within the recovery point objective, for applications with a datastore. One row an application it applies to (applications with a datastore).
A disaster-recovery exercise within the year, for critical applications. One row an application it applies to (critical applications).
Vulnerabilities remediated within thirty days of Patch Tuesday; failing while any is overdue. One row an application it applies to (active applications).
Multi-factor authentication enforced for the application's users. One row an application it applies to (every application).
Access recertified every quarter, for applications with regulated data. One row an application it applies to (applications with regulated data).
Logs shipped to the central sink, covering the application, kept long enough. One row an application it applies to (active applications).
Privileged accounts vaulted, for applications of high or critical criticality. One row an application it applies to (applications of high or critical criticality).
